column3: NKJV includes “It is hard for you to kick against the goads,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text ends with “whom you are persecuting.”

NKJV begins with “So he, trembling and astonished, said, ‘Lord, what do You want me to do?’ Then the Lord said to him,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text begins “But rise and enter the city.”
NKJV has “he saw no one,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “he saw nothing.”
NKJV has the singular “his hand,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has the plural “hands.”
NKJV includes “at once,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text lacks it.
NKJV names “Saul,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “he was with the disciples.”
NKJV has “the Christ,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Jesus.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV supplies “Jesus” in “this Jesus.”
NKJV has “the disciples,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “his disciples.” “Basket” is rendered “large basket.”
NKJV names “Saul,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text has “having arrived.”
NKJV moves “speaking boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus” into verse 29; the Greek has it at the end of verse 28.
NKJV begins with “he spoke boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus,” words the Greek places in verse 28.
